payload.resultSummary:
# Behavioral Spec: `-use-cache` & Misc Details (goimports-reviser v3.0.0)

All probes run on Linux as root, Go 1.21 toolchain in PATH, binary at `/workspace/executable`. Version self-reports:

```
$ /workspace/executable -version          # stdout, exit 0
version: 3.0.0-20260303205914-9926ea38658f
built with: go1.26.0
tag: v3.0.0-20260303205914-9926ea38658f
commit: n/a
source: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/v3
$ /workspace/executable -version-only     # stdout, exit 0, single line WITH trailing \n
3.0.0-20260303205914-9926ea38658f
```

---

## 1. `--help` / `-h` / unknown flag / no args

- `-h`, `--help`, `-help` all behave identically: **exit code 0**, full usage text printed to **stderr only** (stdout empty, usage is 2487 bytes). This is Go `flag` package default behavior.
- Unknown flag: **exit code 2**, stdout empty, stderr is:
  ```
  flag provided but not defined: -bogusflag
  <full usage text, same as --help>
  ```
- No arguments: **exit code 1**, stdout empty, stderr = full usage text followed by a log line:
  ```
  2026/08/10 13:11:46 no file(s) or directory(ies) specified on input
  ```
- Flag forms `-flag`, `--flag`, `-flag=true` all accepted (standard Go flag pkg).
- Exact usage text (stderr, byte-exact from `--help`; note trailing spaces after "your way. \n" lines in `-imports-order` — the multi-line entries end each line with a trailing space before `\n`, visible below as-is):

```
Usage of /workspace/executable:
  -apply-to-generated-files
    	Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter.
  -company-prefixes string
    	Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters.
  -excludes string
    	Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'.
  -file-path string
    	Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line.
  -format
    	Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter.
  -imports-order string
    	Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. 
    	std - std import group; 
    	general - libs for general purpose; 
    	company - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); 
    	project - your local project dependencies;
    	blanked - imports with "_" alias;
    	dotted - imports with "." alias.
    	Optional parameter. (default "std,general,company,project")
  -list-diff
    	Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter.
  -local string
    	Deprecated
  -output string
    	Can be "file", "write" or "stdout". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When "write" together with "-list-diff" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter. (default "file")
  -project-name string
    	Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter.
  -recursive
    	Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter.
  -rm-unused
    	Remove unused imports. Optional parameter.
  -separate-named
    	Option will separate named imports from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter.
  -set-alias
    	Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg "github.com/go-pg/pg/v9"'. Optional parameter.
  -set-exit-status
    	set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter.
  -use-cache
    	Use cache to improve performance. Optional parameter.
  -version
    	Show version information
  -version-only
    	Show only the version string
```

(The description lines are indented with a tab; boolean flags have no ` string` value marker. The 4 lines under `-imports-order` ending in `way. `, `group; `, `purpose; `, `libs); ` have a **trailing space**.)

Note: the binary's name in `Usage of ...` is `os.Args[0]` — when invoked as `/workspace/executable` it prints that path. Also note `-version` help text here says "Show version information" and a `-version-only` flag exists (README is older and lacks `-version-only`).

All log lines go to **stderr** via Go's standard `log` package, format `YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS message`. Normal per-file runs always log:
```
2026/08/10 12:58:01 Paths: [./f.go]
2026/08/10 12:58:01 Processing ./f.go
```
Multiple targets appear space-joined in one bracket: `Paths: [./f.go ./g.go]`. In recursive mode only the dir is logged (`Paths: [.]` / `Processing .`), individual files are NOT logged.

---

## 2. `-use-cache`: location, format, semantics

### 2.1 Cache location
- Directory: `<user-home-from-OS-user-database>/.cache/goimports-reviser/` — as root this is **`/root/.cache/goimports-reviser/`**.
- It does **NOT** honor `$HOME` or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`: ran with `HOME=/tmp/.../fakehome XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/.../fakexdg` — cache still went to `/root/.cache/goimports-reviser/`. Also works under `env -i`. This matches `os/user.Current().HomeDir + "/.cache"` (i.e. `/etc/passwd` lookup), **not** `os.UserCacheDir()`.
- Dir created with perms `0755`, cache files `0644`.
- One cache file per processed source file. No other files (no index, no lock, no logs) are ever written by the tool itself.

### 2.2 Cache file format (verified by md5 computation)
- Filename: lowercase hex **md5 of the cleaned absolute path** of the source file. Verified: `printf '%s' '/tmp/probe/cache/proj1/main.go' | md5sum` = `656b188df0a1ddeb5d3bf32218f09ada` = the created cache filename. `./main.go`, `main.go`, `./sub/../f.go` all map to the same entry (path is made absolute + cleaned, `filepath.Abs` semantics).
- Content: 32 lowercase hex chars = **md5 of the formatted output bytes the tool produced for that file**, **no trailing newline** (file is exactly 32 bytes). Verified: content `9d294fce9a5dff3022301aad1a4e305f` == `md5sum` of the stdout output of the same run. It is NOT the md5 of the input (verified with an unformatted input where input md5 `9a40...` ≠ cache content `68b4...` = output md5).

### 2.3 Skip semantics (all verified experimentally)
On each run, for each explicit file target:
- It computes md5 of the **current file content on disk** and compares with the cached value.
- **Cache hit** (equal): the file is **skipped entirely** — no parsing, **no `go list` subprocesses** (verified with a PATH shim: 0 go calls on hit vs 2 on miss), no write, and — surprisingly — **no stdout output in `-output stdout` mode** (a cache hit in stdout mode prints *nothing* for that file). `Processing <file>` is still logged to stderr. Exit 0.
- **Cache miss**: file is processed normally; if output differs from input the file is rewritten; cache file is (over)written with md5 of the new output.
- **mtime plays no role**: `touch -d 2020-01-01` on a formatted+cached file, rerun with `-use-cache` → still skipped (mtime stayed 2020). Changing content with preserved/old mtime → reprocessed. Purely content-hash based.
- Without `-use-cache`, an explicit file target is **always rewritten** (mtime bumps even when bytes are identical).
- `-list-diff` runs also populate the cache.
- Failed files (parse errors etc.) do NOT create cache entries.
- Cache is never cleaned/TTL'd; entries accumulate forever.

### 2.4 `-use-cache` is silently ignored for directory/recursive targets
- `-use-cache -recursive .` and `-use-cache ./...` on a 201-file tree: **cache directory is not even created**; each run behaves exactly as without cache.
- However, recursive mode has its own built-in no-op detection: unchanged files are NOT rewritten (mtimes preserved) even without `-use-cache` — unlike explicit file targets which are always rewritten without cache.

### 2.5 Cache vs flags: key contains no flags (hazard, verified)
Cache key is path-only, value is output hash of *whatever flags produced last time*. Demonstrated:
1. File with unused `"strings"` import; run `-use-cache ./un.go` → file sorted, import kept, cache = md5(result).
2. Run `-use-cache -rm-unused ./un.go` → **cache hit, processing skipped, unused import NOT removed**, exit 0.
3. Run `-rm-unused ./un.go` (no cache) → import removed.

Conversely no false-positive skip bug: populate cache via `-output stdout` on an unformatted file (cache = md5(formatted output), disk still unformatted), then run `-use-cache` in file mode → file IS rewritten (because md5(disk content) ≠ cache).

### 2.6 Cache error handling
- Cache dir missing → recreated automatically, no message.
- Corrupt cache content (e.g. `echo garbage > <cachefile>`) → treated as miss: file rewritten, cache repaired to correct hash, exit 0, no warning.
- Cache path exists as a **regular file** (mkdir impossible) → **fatal**, exit 1, file NOT processed. stderr:
  ```
  2026/08/10 13:03:19 Paths: [./f.go]
  2026/08/10 13:03:19 Processing ./f.go
  2026/08/10 13:03:19 Failed to create cache directory: mkdir /root/.cache/goimports-reviser: not a directory
  ```
  (Note: `Processing` is logged before the cache-dir creation fails.)

### 2.7 200-file concurrency check
Tree: 201 `.go` files in 10 subdirs, each with unsorted std + project imports. `-recursive .` with and without `-use-cache` produced **byte-identical trees** (`diff -r` clean). Timing: ~0.037s per run without `-rm-unused` (no go calls); no observable ordering artifacts since per-file logging doesn't happen in recursive mode.

---

## 3. stdin

- Target `-` reads the source from **stdin**. Logged as `<standard-input>`:
  ```
  2026/08/10 13:11:46 Paths: [<standard-input>]
  2026/08/10 13:11:46 Processing <standard-input>
  ```
- Output goes to **stdout even in default/`-output file` mode** (there is no file to write). Exit 0.
- Input:
  ```
  package main
  import ("log";"bytes")
  func main(){ var _ = bytes.MinRead; log.Println("x") }
  ```
  Output (stdout):
  ```
  package main

  import (
  	"bytes"
  	"log"
  )

  func main() { var _ = bytes.MinRead; log.Println("x") }
  ```
- With `-use-cache`, a cache entry IS written with key = md5 of the literal string `<standard-input>` (= `2f76bc362b3e399b96be24f616cc3672`), value = md5 of the output. But cache hits are **never honored for stdin**: piping the already-formatted content again with a warm cache still prints the full output (the skip check presumably needs a file to hash before processing).
- stdin still requires project name resolution: from a directory with no `go.mod`, ANY stdin input (even empty/garbage) fails with exit 1, full usage dump on stderr, then:
  ```
  2026/08/10 13:12:46 Could not determine project name for path <standard-input>: open go.mod: no such file or directory
  ```
- With go.mod present: empty stdin → exit 1, stderr ends with:
  ```
  2026/08/10 13:12:56 Failed to fix file: file is empty and cannot be parsed as Go source, use -excludes flag to skip this file: <standard-input>:1:1: expected 'package', found 'EOF'
  ```
  Invalid stdin (`this is not go code`) → exit 1:
  ```
  2026/08/10 13:12:56 Failed to fix file: file has invalid Go source content, use -excludes flag to skip this file: <standard-input>:1:1: expected 'package', found this
  ```
  (For a real file target the same error shows the absolute path, e.g. `... skip this file: /tmp/probe/cache/proj2/bad.go:1:1: expected 'package', found not`.)

---

## 4. `go` subprocess usage (module/package resolution)

Verified with a PATH shim logging argv+cwd of every `go` invocation (delegating to the real go):

- The tool shells out to `go` **only when `-rm-unused` or `-set-alias` is given** (plain run, `-format`, `-use-cache`, `-list-diff` alone → zero go calls).
- Per processed file it runs, **with cwd = the directory containing that file**:
  1. `go list -e -f {{context.ReleaseTags}} -- unsafe`
  2. `go list -e -json=Name,ImportPath,Error,DepOnly,Imports,ImportMap,TestImports,XTestImports -compiled=false -test=true -export=false -deps=true -find=false -pgo=off --`
- This pair runs **once per file** (2 files in same dir → 2 identical pairs; no cross-file caching).
- The child inherits the environment: `GOFLAGS=-tags=mytag` works; `GOFLAGS=-thisisnotaflag` → exit 1 with:
  ```
  2026/08/10 13:07:18 Failed to fix file: err: exit status 1: stderr: go: parsing $GOFLAGS: unknown flag -thisisnotaflag
  ```
  (Note format: `Failed to fix file: err: <err>: stderr: <child stderr>`.)
- `go` not in PATH → exit 1:
  ```
  2026/08/10 13:06:43 Failed to fix file: err: go command required, not found: exec: "go": executable file not found in $PATH: stderr: 
  ```
  (trailing space after `stderr:`).
- Side effect: the child's builds populate `$GOCACHE` (verified: a fresh `GOCACHE` dir got entries). `GOPATH` and `GOMODCACHE` dirs were NOT written in my tests (all deps std/local).
- Package-name resolution for `-rm-unused` comes from `go list`, so `vendor/` and GOPATH-mode resolution work via the go tool itself:
  - Vendored package `example.com/vlib` whose package clause is `package vlibpkg`, used as `vlibpkg.V` → import **kept** (go list resolved name via vendor).
  - GOPATH mode (`GO111MODULE=off GOPATH=...`): `go list` resolves `foo/bar` (`package barpkg`); a file referencing `bar.Y` (wrong qualifier) had the import **removed** as unused — name-based matching against the real package name.
  - `GO111MODULE=off` in a dir WITH go.mod: `-rm-unused` still works (go list is `-e` tolerant).
- **go.mod is mandatory regardless of GO111MODULE**: without go.mod (and without `-project-name`), any run exits 1 with a full usage dump on stderr followed by:
  ```
  2026/08/10 13:07:43 Could not determine project name for path ./m.go: open go.mod: no such file or directory
  ```
  `-project-name myproj` bypasses the go.mod requirement entirely.

---

## 5. Other observations

- **Files the tool writes**: only (a) target `.go` files (file/write output modes) and (b) cache files under `~/.cache/goimports-reviser/` when `-use-cache` with explicit file targets. No log files, no temp files in cwd or /tmp (verified with before/after filesystem snapshots of cwd, HOME, /tmp). The only other filesystem writes observed were the `go list` child's GOCACHE entries.
- `-output write` behaves like `file` (writes back; also populates cache with `-use-cache`).
- `-list-diff` prints the **absolute** path of each differing file to stdout (one per line), e.g. `/tmp/probe/cache/proj2/ld.go`; does not modify the file; repeats the listing on every run even with a warm cache (unformatted file → always a cache miss); exit 0.
- A file whose content is already conforming still gets `Processing ...` logged and (explicit target, no cache) gets rewritten with identical bytes.
- Surprising/quirky items to replicate: cache hit ⇒ **empty stdout** in `-output stdout` mode for that file; `-use-cache` silently ignored for dir/`./...` targets; cache location ignores `HOME`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME` (uses OS user db); cache key ignores flags (stale-skip hazard shown in §2.5).
